title: CUDA Pinned Memory & Stream Patterns - Quick Reference

pinned_memory_allocation.description: Host memory allocation APIs for GPU-accelerated transfers

cudaHostAlloc.signature: cudaError_t cudaHostAlloc(void **pHost, size_t size, unsigned int flags)

parameters.pHost: Output pointer to allocated pinned memory

cudaHostAlloc.performance: 3-10× faster than pageable malloc for transfers

cudaHostRegister.signature: cudaError_t cudaHostRegister(void *p, size_t size, unsigned int flags)

cudaHostAllocDefault.best_for: Most common use case: GPU reads host data

cudaHostAllocWriteCombined.notes: CPU reads from this memory are slow; use for output buffers

cudaHostAllocMapped.best_for: Fine-grained GPU access without explicit copy
cudaHostAllocMapped.warnings: Higher register pressure in kernels, PCIe reads slower than writes

allocation_pattern.startup: Allocate once at app init, large buffers (256MB-1GB)
allocation_pattern.constraints: Max pinned ~10-20% system RAM; limited by OS

cudaMemcpyAsync.signature: cudaError_t cudaMemcpyAsync(void *dst, const void *src, size_t count, cudaMemcpyKind kind, cudaStream_t stream)
cudaMemcpyAsync.gpu_behavior: Copy queued and executed on GPU when stream reaches this operation
cudaMemcpyAsync.ordering: All prior kernels in stream complete before copy; all subsequent kernels wait for copy

cudaMemcpy2DAsync.signature: cudaError_t cudaMemcpy2DAsync(void *dst, size_t dpitch, const void *src, size_t spitch, size_t width, size_t height, cudaMemcpyKind kind, cudaStream_t stream)

cudaMemcpyPeerAsync.signature: cudaError_t cudaMemcpyPeerAsync(void *dst, int dstDev, const void *src, int srcDev, size_t count, cudaStream_t stream)

naive_synchronous.code: cudaMemcpy(host, device, size, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost); kernel(); cudaMemcpy(device, host, size, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice);

bandwidth_optimization.batch_transfers: Queue multiple copies to hide latency
bandwidth_optimization.multiple_streams: Use separate H→D and D→H streams to avoid blocking
bandwidth_optimization.dma_engine_saturation: A100 has 1 copy engine; H100 has 2 (bidirectional)

stream_callbacks.description: Event-driven host work dispatch without polling

cudaLaunchHostFunc.signature: cudaError_t cudaLaunchHostFunc(cudaStream_t stream, cudaHostFn_t function, void *userData)

execution_timing.relative_to_stream: After all prior work in stream completes; before subsequent work
execution_timing.host_thread: Synchronous to stream's host thread (blocks thread during callback)
execution_timing.gpu_thread: GPU doesn't stall; continues other streams

work_stealing.description: Dynamic dispatch of GPU kernels based on completion

cpu_gpu_sync.description: Signal CPU when GPU work completes

conditional_launch.description: Launch next GPU kernel based on previous kernel's results
conditional_launch.benefit: Avoid CPU round-trip, keep data on GPU

callback_chains.description: Chain multiple callbacks for multi-stage pipelines
callback_chains.benefit: Fully asynchronous pipeline without explicit host sync

energy_comparison.polling_approach: CPU busy-wait in tight loop; high power ~10-100W spinning
energy_comparison.callback_approach: CPU parked in scheduler; low power ~2-5W idle

stream_dependencies.description: Ordering and priority control for multi-stream execution

cudaStreamWaitEvent.signature: cudaError_t cudaStreamWaitEvent(cudaStream_t stream, cudaEvent_t event, unsigned int flags)
cudaStreamWaitEvent.gpu_behavior: GPU scheduler checks event at work launch boundary; if not complete, kernel queues (no busy-wait)
cudaStreamWaitEvent.latency: ~100-200 ns GPU scheduler latency to resume after event complete

cudaStreamCreateWithPriority.signature: cudaError_t cudaStreamCreateWithPriority(cudaStream_t *pStream, unsigned int flags, int priority)
cudaStreamCreateWithPriority.preemption: High-priority kernels may preempt low-priority kernels on same SM (context-dependent)

cudaDeviceGetStreamPriorityRange.use_case: Query available priority levels per GPU

linear_chain.parallelism: None; critical path is sum of all kernel times

diamond.description: A → (B, C) → D (parallel middle, converging at end)
diamond.pattern: A(); wait_A in B and C; B(), C() in parallel; wait_B and wait_C in D
diamond.parallelism: B and C overlap; D waits for both

fan_out.pattern: A(); all consumers wait_A in parallel
fan_out.parallelism: All consumers execute in parallel after A completes

complex_dag.description: Arbitrary directed acyclic graph of dependencies
complex_dag.pattern: Multiple wait_events per stream, arbitrary topology
complex_dag.constraints: Must be acyclic to avoid deadlock

pitfall_circular_dependencies.problem: Stream A waits for event from B; B waits for event from A → deadlock
pitfall_circular_dependencies.detection: Nsight profiler shows idle streams; CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 exposes
pitfall_circular_dependencies.prevention: Maintain acyclic topological ordering of stream dependencies

pitfall_lost_events.problem: Stream waits for event that was never recorded
pitfall_lost_events.detection: cudaStreamWaitEvent on unrecorded event; use validation layers
pitfall_lost_events.prevention: Wrapper function enforcing cudaEventRecord before cudaStreamWaitEvent

pitfall_event_reuse.problem: Event reused in new dependency before old dependency completes
pitfall_event_reuse.prevention: Allocate unique event per dependency; use event pool with lifecycle management

pitfall_default_stream.problem: Implicit sync with default stream blocks all operations

pitfall_early_destroy.problem: Destroy event while dependent streams still waiting
pitfall_early_destroy.prevention: Synchronize all dependent streams before cudaEventDestroy()

event_callback_dispatch.advantage: No polling; CPU parks until GPU work done

multi_stage_pipeline.code: kernel_load(); cudaEventRecord(evt_loaded); cudaStreamWaitEvent(compute_stream, evt_loaded); kernel_compute(); cudaEventRecord(evt_computed); cudaStreamWaitEvent(store_stream, evt_computed); kernel_store();

memory: Pre-allocate pinned buffers at startup (avoid fragmentation)
Limit pinned allocation to <20% system RAM
transfers: Always use cudaMemcpyAsync with explicit streams
Queue multiple copies to hide latency
Use separate streams for H→D and D→H to avoid blocking
Measure actual bandwidth with timer events
streams_and_events: Create streams at app startup; destroy at shutdown
Prefer cudaStreamWaitEvent over polling (lower CPU power)
callbacks: Use callbacks for event dispatch, not heavy computation
Consider atomics for thread-safe work queue access
